A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 23-page NileChat paper, including Appendices A-F. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the complete text, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original NileChat evaluations of understanding, translation, cultural knowledge, and value alignment in Section 4, with additional training and model-merging experiments in Figure 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1-2, Figures 3-4, and the experiments reported in Appendices B and D.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain identical translation, persona-controlled generation, retrieval, Qwen2.5-3B continued pretraining, dialect-specific fine-tuning, and model-merging procedures.

E1.justification: The training mixtures in Tables A.1-A.2 and evaluation coverage in Section 4.1 are unchanged, including Egyptian/Moroccan understanding, Palm cultural knowledge, Flores-200 and in-house translation, and WVS value alignment.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in the corresponding main-text and appendix comparisons. This includes Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, the other Arabic-aware LLMs, and NLLB-200-3.3B in translation evaluations.

E3.justification: Both retain zero-/3-shot understanding, zero-/4-shot translation, the same test sample counts and metrics, and Gemma-3-27B cultural-knowledge judging. Training budgets and hyperparameters in Appendix B also match.

E4.justification: Figure 4's pretraining-token analysis, Table B.1's dialect-specific versus merged-model comparison, and Appendix F's correct/incorrect response examples are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis was added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point estimates and averages without reporting repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changed.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative examples match throughout. For example, Table 1 retains NileChat's Egyptian/Moroccan MMLU accuracies of 57.56/57.36, and Table 2 retains its average spBLEU of 21.32. Appendix results also match.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs. The conceptual framework and mathematical descriptions are identical, with no added or revised definitions, formal assumptions, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same augmentation framework, corpus/model release contributions, and claims about NileChat's dialectal and cultural capabilities relative to comparable and larger models.

C2.justification: The cultural-alignment interpretations in Section 4.2 and cross-dialect transfer explanation in Appendix B.2 are unchanged. Both retain the same limitations concerning teacher dependency, translated SFT data, hallucination, computational cost, safety alignment, and subtle cultural nuances.

D1.justification: Data recipes, filtering, hardware, training times, hyperparameters, and Appendix E's prompt templates are identical. Reported code/data/model access information and the repository link destination are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the complete reference list match. The positioning relative to translation-based augmentation, cultural adaptation, and existing Arabic LLMs is unchanged.

P1.justification: The only textual edit is the marginal arXiv stamp, changing from v1 dated 23 May 2025 to v2 dated 11 September 2025. The title, authors, body wording, and section/appendix organization remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1-10 and all main-text and appendix tables retain their styling, captions, structure, and placement. Negligible PDF text-position differences do not change the page layout or visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Apart from the arXiv version/date stamp and its version-specific link, v2 preserves v1's scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, limitations, and presentation. These administrative updates produce no meaningful gain or loss in overall paper quality.
